# BELL YARD VOICES

## Project
- Subject: Bell Yard Hall, Bell Yard
- Treatment: chronological oral history opening
- Audience: local history documentary viewers
- Viewing context: community screening and documentary streaming
- Tone: attentive, intimate, grounded in the changing hall
- Film title: BELL YARD VOICES
- Tagline: A street remembers
- Duration: 15 seconds
- Shot count: 6
- Main frame: 16:9
- Future adaptation frame: 9:16

steps.userMessage:
BELL YARD VOICES | An oral history documentary opening

We are preparing a local history documentary about Bell Yard Hall. Design its 15-second opening as six shots, moving through 1938, 1964, 1991 and 2018 before a present-day illustration and the title. The four photographs establish the chronology; Ruth Cole's recorded memories carry the story. Print "BELL YARD VOICES" and "A street remembers" on the final title frame.

The archive contains photographs taken at Bell Yard Hall, Bell Yard, on 12 June 1938 by Arthur Bell, 8 September 1964 by Joan Mercer, 21 November 1991 by Peter Shaw and 14 April 2018 by Helen Cole. All four are cleared for film and promotion, with photographer credit required. The hall's five upper windows, central arched doorway and circular gable vent connect the decades. Ruth appears in the 2018 photograph; her short silver bob, round dark glasses and navy cardigan also identify her in the present-day drawing. The opening uses a 16:9 frame. The attached geometry also establishes a 9:16 frame for future adaptations, with action margins of 3.5% and graphics margins of 5% on every edge in both proportions.

Audience: local history documentary viewers, with the director and community history group using this work to approve the opening's chronology, portrayal and edit.

Inputs (attached): 01-client-facts.en.md contains the project facts. 02-delivery-catalog.en.md lists each deliverable's proportion, format and stage. 03-archive-register.en.md records photograph dates, locations, credits, permissions and camera positions. 04-interview-transcript.en.md supplies Ruth's exact words and the description cue. 05-opening-timeline.en.md fixes the six shot intervals and source order. frame-and-caption-geometry.png defines safe areas and text zones. bell-yard-plan.png locates the hall and four archive viewpoints. archive-1938.png supplies the opening-day photograph. archive-1964.png supplies the tea-day photograph. archive-1991.png supplies the closure photograph. archive-2018.png supplies the reopening photograph and Ruth's appearance. bell-yard-today.png supplies present-day daylight and material atmosphere.

Deliverables:
1. A one-page shot and archive specification covering six shots, source records, shot sizes, actions, dialogue, character names and the 15-second timeline
2. One Ruth Cole character sheet with front, side and back views, three expressions and her three identifying features
3. Four archive treatment studies, one per photograph, showing the source image, proposed crop, movement and complete attribution
4. Two consecutive storyboard pages, three shots per page, with shot annotations, archive or illustration labels and subtitle placeholders inside each frame
5. Two finished keyframes for S04 and S05, showing the photographic treatment and present-day illustration respectively
6. One text and sound cue sheet covering all six shots, the four interview excerpts, attribution text, subtitle intervals and the description gap
7. One final title frame carrying the film name and tagline
8. One 15-second animatic of all six shots with interview audio, subtitles and the final title
9. One presentation document of at least eight pages, reusing the specification, character sheet, archive studies, storyboards, keyframes, cue sheet and title, with a shot-by-shot account of the fixed facts

Acceptance:
- The specification, both storyboard pages, cue sheet, animatic and presentation repeat six shots and 15 seconds: S01–S04 last 3 seconds each, S05–S06 last 1.5 seconds each. Their source order is A01, A02, A03, A04, present-day illustration, title.
- The four archive studies, archive storyboard frames, S04 keyframe and animatic print "Archive", the corresponding full date, Bell Yard Hall, Bell Yard, and the photographer's name introduced by "Photograph by". Their source entries match 03-archive-register.en.md. The S05 storyboard frame, keyframe and animatic print "Illustration" throughout the drawn shot.
- The character sheet, S05 storyboard frame and S05 keyframe retain Ruth's short silver bob, round dark glasses and navy cardigan from A04. The archive studies and S05 drawing preserve the hall's five upper windows, central arched doorway and circular gable vent wherever those features enter the frame; their viewpoints follow bell-yard-plan.png.
- Every storyboard frame prints its shot ID, one shot size from WS, MS or CU, duration in seconds and character entry: None for S01–S03 and S06, Ruth Cole for S04–S05. The specification and cue sheet carry matching entries. Storyboards, keyframes, title and animatic use the 16:9 safe areas; archive labels occupy the upper band at 5–18% of frame height and subtitles occupy the lower zone at 78–93%, within the attached horizontal bounds.
- The cue sheet and animatic reproduce T01–T04 from 04-interview-transcript.en.md word for word in audio and subtitles, one excerpt per corresponding archive shot. Subtitles use at most two lines, centered below, with each cue lasting 3 seconds. S05 reserves 1.5 seconds between interview and title for D01 in the description track.
- The title frame, animatic's final 1.5 seconds and presentation cover print "BELL YARD VOICES" and "A street remembers". The presentation contains at least eight pages and locates the chronology, attribution, illustration label, Ruth's three features and subtitle timing by shot ID.

Please clearly mark which version you consider the final deliverable. If nothing is marked, the last exported version counts.
